notation.meaning: Effect of treatment (per unit of $D_i$ if continuous)
Unit fixed effect: everything permanent about unit $i$

blocks.md: **When China joined the WTO and the US granted it permanent normal trade relations (PNTR), the threat of tariffs jumping back to Smoot-Hawley levels disappeared. Industries where that threat had been largest — the biggest "NTR gap" — lost the most employment afterwards, and the losses kept growing through 2007.**

- Since 1980 US imports from China paid the low Normal Trade Relations (NTR) tariffs reserved for WTO members — but only through **annual renewals** that were uncertain and politically contentious.
- Without renewal, tariffs would jump to the much higher non-NTR rates (Smoot-Hawley, 1930).
- With China's WTO accession, the US granted PNTR (effective 2001), removing that risk.
- The size of the risk varied by industry: $\text{NTR Gap}_i = \text{Non-NTR rate}_i - \text{NTR rate}_i$.

blocks.md: NTR gaps across manufacturing industries in 1999 peak around 0.35; the 25th percentile is 0.23 and the 75th 0.40.
Newspaper coverage of China's NTR status spiked in the early 1990s and again around 2000, then vanished after PNTR.

OLS on industry-year log employment, 1990–2007: $\ln(\text{Emp}_{it}) = \theta\,\text{Post}_t \times \text{NTRGap}_i + \text{Post}_t \times \mathbf{X}_i'\gamma + \mathbf{X}_{it}'\lambda + \delta_t + \delta_i + \alpha + \varepsilon_{it}$, with industry and year fixed effects, weighted by 1990 employment, standard errors clustered by industry ([Difference-in-Differences](note:difference-in-differences)).

**Magnitude**: moving an industry from the 25th (0.23) to the 75th (0.40) percentile NTR gap implies a relative employment loss of $-0.47 \times (0.40 - 0.23) = -0.08$ log points.

blocks.alt: PNTR effect on US manufacturing employment event study

blocks.md: With baseline controls, the year-by-year coefficients are near zero before 2001 and turn negative right after PNTR; by 2007 the 90% confidence interval is roughly −0.25 to −1.1 (read off the chart). Without controls the decline is steeper. **The effect is felt quickly, and it grows over time.**

- **Identification from uncertainty**: tariffs did not actually fall in 2001; what changed was the removal of the risk that they would rise. Industries with large gaps gained most certainty, encouraging firms to invest in Chinese supply chains.
- **Relative effects**: the design compares high- and low-gap industries; it does not measure the aggregate fall in manufacturing.
- **Pre-trends**: flat pre-2001 coefficients support parallel trends.
